mainTopic: Carrying on roofs on שבת: combining a roof with an אכסדרה or a ruin, and the dispute of רב and שמואל about a single roof and a ship
overview: This amud begins with the end of an answer from the previous amud: a certain structure was built to guard a garden, not to reach the roofs. רמי בר חמא then asks about carrying two אמות on a roof and two אמות on a pillar. רבה objects that this is obvious, since a roof is a כרמלית and the pillar is a רשות היחיד. So the גמרא explains that the real question was about a roof and an אכסדרה, which is not fit to live in. רב ביבי בר אביי asks a similar question about a roof and a ruin. He explains that a ruin, unlike an אכסדרה, is fit to live in, even though no one lives there now. That question ends with תיקו, unresolved. Next, רב and שמואל disagree about carrying on a single roof: רב allows the whole roof, and שמואל allows only four אמות. The גמרא settles each one's apparent self-contradiction, using noticeable walls for רב and the size of the roof (more than two בית סאה, like a קרפף not enclosed for living) for שמואל. Finally, the same two argue about carrying on a ship, and the explanation of רב's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The structure was built to guard the garden
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of an answer from the previous discussion. The structure in question was built to guard a garden. It was not built to give access to the roofs, so it does not affect רב's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was made to guard the garden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous section. It explains that a certain building was made only to watch over a garden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone had tried to use this structure to challenge the הלכה about roofs. The answer pushes the challenge away by explaining what the structure was actually for. Since it was built to guard the garden and not to connect to the roofs, it does not change the הלכה.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is the tail end of an answer that began on the previous page.

phrases.english: to guard the garden
is what it was made for.
phrases.notes: It was not made to give access to the roofs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a defense that began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The structure seemed to show that roofs can be connected for carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: The structure served only to guard the garden, so it proves nothing about the roofs.

steps.title: Two אמות on a roof and two on a pillar
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks a question that follows רב's rule of four אמות on roofs. What if someone carries two אמות on a roof and two אמות on a nearby pillar?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: if someone carries two אמות on a roof and two אמות on a pillar, what is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רמי בר חמא asks whether the four-אמות limit can be filled by two אמות on a roof plus two on a pillar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, a person on the roofs may carry only within four אמות. The question is whether the pillar joins the roof to make one four-אמות area. The pillar is ten טפחים high and four טפחים wide.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
two cubits on a roof
phrases.notes: Half of the four-cubit limit.

phrases.english: and two cubits on a pillar, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Does the pillar combine with the roof?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question that builds on רב's rule about roofs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can two אמות on a roof combine with two אמות on a pillar for carrying?

steps.title: רבה says the answer is obvious
steps.stepSummary: רבה objects to the question itself. The roof is a כרמלית and the pillar is a רשות היחיד. Carrying between them is clearly forbidden, so there is nothing to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What is he asking? Is he asking about a כרמלית and a רשות היחיד?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה challenges the question. He says it has an obvious answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is worded as a question, but it is really an attack. A roof counts as a כרמלית. A pillar ten טפחים high and four wide is a רשות היחיד. Everyone knows you may not carry between those two domains, so asking about it makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: what is he asking? (meaning: this is obvious)
an in-between domain where the רבנן forbade carrying

steps.confusionAlert: Even though רבה's words are a question, he is not asking for information. He is saying the question is pointless.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
what is he asking about?
phrases.notes: רבה isn't really asking; he's challenging the question.

phrases.english: a karmelit and a private domain
phrases.notes: The roof is the karmelit and the pillar is the private domain.

phrases.english: is he asking about?
phrases.notes: Of course carrying between them is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the question asked in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's question about the roof and the pillar
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The roof and the pillar are two different domains, a כרמלית and a רשות היחיד. Carrying between them is obviously forbidden, so the question has no room.

steps.title: The real question: a roof and an אכסדרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רמי בר חמא worded his question imprecisely because of his quick mind. His real question was about two אמות on a roof and two אמות on an אכסדרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of his sharpness, רמי בר חמא did not look carefully at his wording. Rather, this is what he was asking: two אמות on a roof and two אמות on an אכסדרה, what is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבה by fixing the wording of the question. The pillar is swapped for an אכסדרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אכסדרה is a roofed porch with no walls. Its roof, unlike the pillar, is not a רשות היחיד, so רבה's objection no longer applies. Now the question is real: can the roof and the אכסדרה count as one area?

keyTerms.meaning: because of his sharpness (he thought so fast he was not precise)
he did not look into it carefully

steps.whatToRemember: The question was never about a pillar. It was about a roof next to an אכסדרה.

phrases.english: and Rami bar Chama, because of his sharpness,
phrases.notes: Explains why the wording was off.

phrases.english: did not examine it carefully;
phrases.notes: He was not precise in his wording.

phrases.english: rather, this is what he was asking:
two cubits on a roof
phrases.notes: The same first half as before.

phrases.english: and two cubits on a portico, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The pillar is replaced by a portico.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge by correcting the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question seemed to be about a roof and a pillar, which has an obvious answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real question is about a roof and an אכסדרה, which has no obvious answer.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both sides. Maybe the roof and the אכסדרה are one domain, since neither is fit to live in. Or maybe carrying between them is forbidden, just as carrying from roof to roof is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that since neither this one nor that one is fit to live in, they are one domain? Or perhaps, since carrying from roof to roof is forbidden, carrying from a roof to an אכסדרה is also forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the sides of רמי בר חמא's question. It lists one reason to allow carrying and one reason to forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: neither the roof nor the אכסדרה is a place where people live, so they may count as one domain. Side two: רב forbids carrying from one roof to another, so a roof and an אכסדרה may also be separate domains. The discussion that follows ends with תיקו in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: do we say? (introduces the first side)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that whether a place is used for living can decide whether two areas count as one domain for carrying.

phrases.english: Do we say:
since neither is this fit for living in
phrases.notes: The roof.

phrases.english: nor is this fit for living in
phrases.notes: The portico.

phrases.english: it is one domain.
phrases.notes: So carrying between them would be allowed.

phrases.english: Or perhaps:
since from roof to roof is forbidden,
phrases.notes: Follows רב's rule.

phrases.english: from roof to portico is also forbidden.
phrases.notes: The portico is treated like a separate roof.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הַאי חֲזֵי לְדִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the corrected question from step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are a roof and an אכסדרה one domain because neither is used for living, or separate domains like two roofs?

steps.title: Carrying between a roof and a ruin
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי asks a new question. What if someone carries two אמות on a roof and two אמות in a ruin?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי asked: two אמות on a roof and two אמות in a ruin, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא asks a question that looks like רמי בר חמא's question. This time the second place is a ruin (חורבה) instead of an אכסדרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has the same shape as before. Half the carrying is on a roof and half is in another area. The only change is the second area, which is now a ruined house. The next steps will ask whether that change makes any difference.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (introduces a real question or dilemma)
A ruin, a house that has collapsed

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye asked:
two cubits on a roof
and two cubits in a ruin, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Picture the roof of a ruin that belongs to someone else, with one side open to the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question, modeled on רמי בר חמא's question about the אכסדרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can one combine two אמות on a roof with two אמות in a ruin, or is it forbidden to carry between them?

steps.title: Isn't this the same as רמי בר חמא's question?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא objects. This question seems identical to the one רמי בר חמא already asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Isn't this exactly רמי בר חמא's question?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges the new question as repetitive. He says it is the same as the earlier question about an אכסדרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on the need for the question, not on any law. If a ruin and an אכסדרה work the same way, then רב ביבי has added nothing new.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Is this not the same as Rami bar Ḥama's question?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 6 is a new question at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב ביבי בר אביי's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruin seems no different from an אכסדרה, so the question was already asked by רמי בר חמא.

steps.title: A ruin is fit to live in, unlike an אכסדרה
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי says he is not just copying an old question. An אכסדרה is not fit to live in, but a ruin is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: Did I come late just to pick a fight? An אכסדרה is not fit for living in, but a ruin is fit for living in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי defends his question. He points to a real difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, one side of the question said the roof and the אכסדרה might count as one area because neither is fit to live in. A ruin can be rebuilt and lived in, so that reason may not work for it. That difference is what makes the question new.

keyTerms.meaning: A portico, a roofed area open on the sides

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
And did I come late just to quarrel?
phrases.notes: Wordplay: מאחר means 'late' and also hints at 'from another', as if he were meddling in someone else's question.

phrases.english: A portico is not fit for living in,
while a ruin is fit for living in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge by drawing a distinction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ruin is the same as an אכסדרה, so the question is a repeat.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ruin is fit for living, an אכסדרה is not, so the cases may differ.

steps.title: If it is fit to live in, what is the question?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. If a ruin is fit to live in, it should be like a regular roof area, and carrying should simply be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is fit for living in, what is his question?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רב ביבי's own distinction against him. Now there seems to be nothing left to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason to allow carrying was that the area is not fit to live in. If a ruin is fit to live in, it should be like carrying from roof to roof, which is forbidden. So the answer seems obvious.

phrases.english: And since it is fit for living in,
what is he asking about!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּחַזְיָא לְדִירָה מַאי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The validity of the question once the ruin is called fit for living
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being fit for living makes the ruin like a roof-to-roof case, which is clearly forbidden. So there is no doubt left.

steps.title: The question is asked in an 'if you say' style
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב ביבי's question builds on top of רמי בר חמא's. Even if an אכסדרה is permitted, maybe a ruin is different. Or maybe not, since no one lives in it right now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is speaking in the style of 'if you say'. If you say that an אכסדרה, which is not fit for living, is permitted, what about a ruin, which is fit for living? Or perhaps, right now at least, no one lives in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies how the question works. It is a follow-up that only applies if we first permit the אכסדרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step one: assume an אכסדרה is permitted because it is not fit for living. Step two: ask whether a ruin's potential to be lived in forbids it. Or maybe what counts is that no one lives there right now, so it is permitted like the אכסדרה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you conclude that... (a follow-up question that builds on an earlier answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רב ביבי repeating רמי בר חמא's question. His question only starts after you assume the אכסדרה is permitted.

phrases.english: He is speaking in an 'if you say' style:
If you say
that a portico is not fit for living in (and so carrying is permitted),
a ruin is fit for living in (so is it forbidden)?
Or perhaps:
right now, at least, there are no residents in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by explaining that the question builds on רמי בר חמא's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the question as a follow-up
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being fit for living makes the ruin obviously forbidden, so there is nothing to ask.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt is whether we follow the ruin's potential to be lived in or the fact that no one lives there now.

steps.title: The question remains unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question about the ruin is left unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether a ruin's potential to be lived in matters, or only the fact that it is empty right now. So the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand, the question is unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: A roof plus an אכסדרה, and a roof plus a ruin, are open questions. The ruin question hinges on whether we look at potential living or at actual living right now.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question opened in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of carrying between a roof and a ruin is unresolved.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about carrying on level roofs or a single roof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic: level roofs according to רבי מאיר, or a single roof according to the רבנן. רב allows carrying throughout the whole roof. שמואל allows only four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Level roofs according to רבי מאיר, and a single roof according to the רבנן: רב said one may carry throughout all of it. שמואל said one may carry in it only within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. רב and שמואל disagree about how far one may carry on these roofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats level roofs as one shared area. The רבנן treat each roof as its own area, but here the roof stands alone. רב treats the whole area as usable for carrying. שמואל limits carrying to four אמות. Step 16 explains his reason: the roof is larger than two בית סאה, and its walls were built for the house below, not for the roof. So it is like a קרפף that was not enclosed for living.

keyTerms.meaning: To carry or move an object

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute sets up the coming discussion of whether roofs without walls count as properly enclosed areas.

phrases.english: Level roofs according to Rabbi Meir,
and a single roof according to the Rabbis,
Rav said:
It is permitted to carry throughout all of it,
and Shmuel said:
One may carry in it only within four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּגִּין הַשָּׁוִין לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְגַג יְחִידִי לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: one may carry throughout the whole roof. שמואל: one may carry only within four אמות.

steps.title: רב seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב's ruling that one may carry on the whole roof and points out that it seems to clash with what רב said earlier about level roofs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: it is permitted to carry on the whole roof. This is difficult, because one statement of רב contradicts another statement of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב's ruling from the previous step in order to attack it. Earlier, about level roofs according to the רבנן, רב allowed carrying only four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With level roofs according to the רבנן, רב was strict and limited carrying to four אמות on each roof. Here, with a single roof (or level roofs according to רבי מאיר), he is lenient and allows carrying everywhere. Since both cases involve carrying on a roof, the גמרא asks why רב ruled differently.

keyTerms.meaning: One statement of רב contradicts another statement of רב
To carry or move an object
Throughout the whole of it (the whole roof)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion of רב. The גמרא is quoting the ruling from step 12 again so that it can question it.

phrases.english: Rav said: it is permitted to carry throughout all of it,
phrases.notes: Repeated from the previous step in order to challenge it

phrases.english: Rav contradicts Rav!
phrases.notes: Refers to his stricter ruling about level roofs

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from step 12 by comparing it with his earlier ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's lenient ruling on a single roof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב was strict with level roofs (only four אמות) but lenient here, which looks inconsistent.

steps.title: Inner walls are not noticeable, outer walls are
steps.stepSummary: With level roofs, the walls between the houses cannot be seen from above. With a single house, the outer walls are clearly noticeable.
steps.simpleTranslation: There (level roofs according to the רבנן), the partitions are not noticeable. Here (a single roof, or level roofs according to רבי מאיר), the partitions are noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are different. It depends on whether the walls below can be noticed from the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a row of level roofs, the inner walls between the houses are not noticeable, so we do not treat them as rising up to mark off each roof. On a single house (or a group of level roofs according to רבי מאיר), the outer walls are noticeable at the roof's edge, so they count as partitions around the roof. That allows carrying on the whole roof.

phrases.english: There, the partition is not noticeable.
phrases.notes: The inner walls between level roofs

phrases.english: Here, the outer partition is noticeable.
phrases.notes: The outer walls of a single house

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases are roofs, so the ruling should be the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: A noticeable outer wall counts as a partition for the roof. Hidden inner walls do not.

steps.title: שמואל seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes שמואל's strict ruling for a single roof and points out that it seems to clash with his lenient ruling about level roofs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: one may carry on it only within four אמות. This is difficult, because one statement of שמואל contradicts another statement of שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא does the same thing to שמואל. Earlier, about level roofs according to the רבנן, שמואל allowed carrying throughout each separate roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's pattern is the opposite of רב's. He was lenient with level roofs but is strict with a single roof. If the single roof is even better enclosed, the גמרא asks why it should be stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, the small area where one may always carry
One statement of שמואל contradicts another statement of שמואל

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: one may not carry on it
phrases.notes: Repeated from step 12 in order to challenge it

phrases.english: except within four cubits,
Shmuel contradicts Shmuel!
phrases.notes: Refers to his lenient ruling about level roofs

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel challenge, now aimed at שמואל instead of רב
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's strict ruling on a single roof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל was lenient with level roofs but strict here, which looks inconsistent.

steps.title: Size matters: a big roof is like an unlived-in enclosure
steps.stepSummary: The level roofs were not bigger than two בית סאה, but this roof is. Its walls were built for the house below, not for the roof, so it is like a large קרפף not enclosed for living, where one may carry only four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the roof was not bigger than two בית סאה. Here, it is bigger than two בית סאה. These walls were made for the house below, not for the roof above. So the roof is like a קרפף bigger than two בית סאה that was not enclosed for living. In any such enclosure, one may carry only within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers שמואל's contradiction by pointing to the size of the roof. It then explains why size changes the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small area (up to two בית סאה) with partitions is fine for carrying. A larger area is fine only if it was enclosed for living. The house walls were built to serve the rooms below, not the roof. So the large roof counts as an area not enclosed for living, and carrying is limited to four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of two בית סאה (5,000 square אמות), the size of the courtyard of the משכן
An enclosed open area, like a storage yard, outside the house
That was not enclosed for the purpose of living there
They were made for use below

steps.whatToRemember: רב's two rulings fit together because noticeable walls count. שמואל's two rulings fit together because of size: over two בית סאה, walls not built for the roof count only like a קרפף not enclosed for living.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the general rule of a קרפף larger than two בית סאה, which appears throughout מסכת עירובין.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, לָא הָוֵי יוֹתֵר מִבֵּית סָאתַיִם.
phrases.english: There, it is not more than two beit se'a.
phrases.notes: The level roofs in the earlier case

phrases.english: Here, it is more than two beit se'a,
and these partitions were made for below,
phrases.notes: For the house itself

phrases.english: they were not made for above,
phrases.notes: Not for the roof

phrases.english: and it is like an enclosure larger than two beit se'a
that was not enclosed for residence,
and any enclosure larger than two beit se'a
that was not enclosed for residence —
one may carry in it only within four (cubits).

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, לָא הָוֵי יוֹתֵר מִבֵּית סָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by size and purpose of the walls
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases are roofs, so שמואל should rule the same way in both.
steps.terutzMaskana: A roof bigger than two בית סאה, with walls not built for it, has the status of a קרפף not enclosed for living. Only four אמות are allowed.

steps.title: The same dispute about a ship
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל argue in the same way about carrying on a ship. רב allows the whole ship, and שמואל allows only four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about a ship: רב said it is permitted to carry throughout the whole ship. שמואל said one may carry on it only within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related dispute between the same two אמוראים, this time about a large ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The positions match their roof dispute. רב is lenient and treats the ship as one enclosed area. שמואל is strict and limits carrying to four אמות. The reasons for each view are explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)

phrases.english: It was stated: a ship.
Rav said: it is permitted to carry throughout all of it,
and Shmuel said: one may not carry in it
except within four (cubits).

steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: it is permitted to carry throughout the whole ship —

steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new has been added yet. Quoting the ruling again marks the shift from stating the dispute to explaining it.
